messages:
alex: quick heads-up — CI started failing after the poetry lock bump; root cause looks like a new tokenizers wheel that triggers a C-extension build on musl images. CVE report referenced below.

mira: repro steps? which job is dying?

alex: failing job is `tests:py38-linux` on our shared runner. error is `failed to build wheel for tokenizers` and then pip falls back to source build. logs: ```
  ERROR: Failed building wheel for tokenizers
  running build_ext
  clang: error: linker command failed with exit code 1
```

sam: ugh. we hit this last quarter — manylinux wheel was removed for 0.xx.y. Are we pinned in constraints.txt?
\ajen: our poetry.lock had updated to `tokenizers 0.13.5` from the last `0.13.3` we pinned. constraints.txt was regenerated but not checked into the runner image.

kyle: the stack in CI uses an alpine-based image for some matrix entries (musl). That forces a source build. If the CVE needs immediate attention we should either pin the wheel to a safe version or switch job to manylinux-based image.

sec-bot: [VULN] CVE-2026-8731 affecting tokenizers < 0.13.5: potential buffer overflow in C extension. Severity: High. Patch available in 0.13.5. More details: https://vuln-db.example/CVE-2026-8731

mira: so 0.13.5 fixes the CVE but causes source builds on musl that fail — we need a short-term mitigation that keeps us secure without breaking CI. Options: pin to 0.13.3 (vulnerable) + backport patch (not realistic), rebuild manylinux wheels and host internally, or change CI images.

sam: can we vendor a prebuilt wheel into our test env? that's quick for CI only.

alex: proposal: 1) immediate: pin tokenizers==0.13.5 in poetry.lock AND add wheel-based install in CI by switching that job to ubuntu:22.04 image (manylinux) so pip pulls a wheel. 2) midterm: add a post-submit job that builds and uploads our internal manylinux wheels for reproducibility. 3) longterm: add constraint policy that avoids unverified source builds on musl for security-sensitive packages.

jen: +1 for the immediate switch. Changing the job image is lowest risk and preserves CVE fix. I'll open PR to mutate the workflow matrix.

kyle: I can take the CI change. also will add a check that fails early if `pip` would fall back to building from source: `pip download --no-binary :all: tokenizers==0.13.5` should tell us.

sam: note on packaging: transformers >=4.36 picks up tokenizers optional C flags, may force build. We should run our test matrix with transformers 4.35.x and 4.36.x to verify.

mira: action items: alex to open poetry.lock PR; jen/kyle adjust CI matrix; sam run compatibility sweep; I'll own backport plan if we need to pin older versions for specific customers.

alex: opening PR now: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood/pull/5821 — updates poetry.lock to pin tokenizers==0.13.5 and adds note in changelog about CVE.

jen: CI matrix change PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood/pull/5822 — switches `tests:py38-linux` to ubuntu runner for wheel installs.

sam: I'm running a quick compat job locally against both transformers 4.35.2 and 4.36.0, will post results in this thread. :eyes:

sec-bot: [INFO] Created internal vuln ticket INFSEC-4467 and assigned to eng-security.

kyle: also throwing this on the dedicated infra checklist — any wheel we rely on should have reproducible builds and a KMS-signed artifact if we ship to Dedicated. Not urgent here but noted.

mira: good call on KMS signatures — add to roadmap for Dedicated/Private.

sam: quick update: transformers 4.36.0 + tokenizers 0.13.5 passes our unit tests locally on ubuntu runner. On alpine it still fails due to missing build deps (rust/cargo).

alex: for now we'll merge the lock + CI job change, mark the regression as `P2` for the non-ubuntu runners, and schedule an infra ticket to either provide prebuilt wheels or install proper build toolchain in the alpine images.

jen: merged lock PR and CI change — both green on the ubuntu matrices. shipping the CVE fix to prod apps now. :shipit:

mira: I'll create INFSEC follow-ups: one to track internal wheel hosting (INFSEC-4468) and one about KMS signing for Dedicated artifacts (INFSEC-4469).

alex: thanks everyone. after we close these follow-ups we'll add a short blurb to the release notes about the CVE and the CI mitigation steps. :thumbsup:
